title: Whose are these? Kenen …?
summary: Ask whose several things are using an unsuffixed plural noun and nämä ovat.
prerequisiteSkills: Plural possessed nouns in ownership sentences
objectives: Ask whose several things are using an unsuffixed plural noun and nämä ovat.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: Ask about an unspecified owner
paragraphs: Kenen means “whose”, an owner-question form of kuka (“who”). The owner is unspecified, so add no personal possessive suffix.
Use Kenen + plural noun + nämä ovat?: Kenen pallot nämä ovat? (“Whose balls are these?”). Keep plural -t without a possessive suffix. Kenen nämä pallot ovat? is also ordinary word order.
Kenen does not establish how many people own the thing or things. Explicit questions about several owners are outside this pattern. Typed and token tasks accept both taught word orders.
keyPoints: no personal suffix on the question noun

steps: Begin with Kenen (“whose”) to ask about an unspecified owner.
Use kirjat (“books”) without a personal possessive suffix.
Use nämä ovat for the several things being identified.

commonMistakes: Do not add a personal suffix to the question noun.
The number of things does not determine the number of owners.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: kenen + unsuffixed plural noun + nämä + ovat

parts.formation: Kenen is the owner-question form of kuka (“who”). Several things do not by themselves change kenen.
talo + -t = talot. No personal owner is named, so keep -t and add no personal possessive suffix.
Nämä is the plural of tämä and identifies several things.
Use ovat with plural nämä; begin the owner question with kenen, without onko.
